target.title: fix(codex): rename destructive approval mode to ask
target.body:
Closes #98499

Related: #97123
Related: #97327

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring Codex plugin write/destructive approvals had to use the value `"always"` even though the behavior asks the user for every action. The contradictory name makes the approval contract easy to misread and can lead operators to make incorrect permission assumptions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex plugin contract now uses `"ask"` across the manifest, public types, runtime policy, persisted binding shape, migration contracts, examples, tests, and documentation. This is an intentional hard cut: `"always"` fails validation and is neither aliased nor migrated.

`"ask"` preserves the existing fail-closed behavior for durable per-tool approval overrides and carries the human reviewer through thread start/resume, turn start, and side-thread fork. Per-app policy context remains authoritative in the elicitation bridge, so mixed `true`, `false`, `"auto"`, and `"ask"` configurations do not broaden sibling app permissions.

AI-assisted: yes. Codex implemented the change and completed a clean current-main repository autoreview.

## User Impact

Operators can express the behavior directly with `allow_destructive_actions: "ask"`: destructive plugin actions remain available but require user approval every time. Existing boolean and `"auto"` policies are unchanged. Old configurations using `"always"` must be updated and will now fail validation instead of being silently accepted or migrated.

## Evidence

- Current-main focused validation passed: 4 files, 6 tests passed, 286 skipped by the targeted filter.
- Task-file formatting passed for all changed files.
- `git diff --cached --check` passed before commit.
- Fresh current-main autoreview completed cleanly with no accepted or actionable findings.
- Direct sibling Codex source inspection confirmed that `approvalsReviewer` is supported on thread start/resume/fork and turn start and persists into subsequent-turn session configuration.
- The broad extension typecheck reached an unrelated current-main QA Lab error: `extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.ts` references missing `providerUrl` and `providerHeaders` fields. No Codex task file was reported.
- Exact-head CI passed the Codex/task-relevant tests, production types, docs, formatting, dependency, security, and boundary checks. Three leaves failed only in files outside this PR: `src/llm/providers/mistral.test.ts` saw the test value redacted to `***`; `src/gateway/server-cron.test.ts` had two existing lint errors; and gateway/Anthropic tests had four existing test-type errors. The PR diff does not touch those files, and the gateway failures are present in the exact base commit `b9ae0a76fa` from #96711.

Commands:

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-codex-plugin-destructive-ask-vitest node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts src/config/config.plugin-validation.test.ts -t 'keeps ask plugin policy|passes session plugin app policy context|accepts ask destructive policy|rejects old always destructive policy'

node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 -- <23 changed files>

OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-codex-plugin-destructive-ask-extensions.tsbuildinfo

.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --prompt '<task-scoped current-main review>' --stream-engine-output
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Replace the misleading Codex plugin destructive-action string `"always"` with `"ask"`, reject the retired value, and keep human approval routing effective across every thread/turn entry point.
- **Real environment tested:** Current `origin/main` at `15bb4874bf` in an isolated macOS worktree, using the repository Vitest wrapper and the checked-out sibling Codex source contract.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Applied the task-only patch onto current `origin/main`, resolved the moved side-thread fork reviewer line to the `ask`-aware resolver, ran the four-file targeted Vitest command above, checked all changed files with `oxfmt`, ran `git diff --cached --check`, and completed a fresh local autoreview.
- **Evidence after fix:** The targeted tests prove that `"ask"` is accepted, `"always"` is rejected at both global and per-plugin config paths, the human reviewer survives initial thread setup and first turn, the same routing is used for side-thread forks, and adjacent Codex plugin configuration remains intact. All 6 selected cases passed.
- **Observed result after fix:** The schema and runtime expose only `true`, `false`, `"auto"`, and `"ask"`; old `"always"` configurations fail rather than normalize. `"ask"` routes to the human reviewer while each app's effective policy is still enforced independently by the elicitation bridge.
- **What was not tested:** No live gateway, Slack approval card, deploy, publish, or service restart was performed. The full local suite was not run. The current-main extension typecheck was blocked by the unrelated QA Lab errors listed above; exact-head CI also exposed three unrelated base failures outside the PR diff. Focused Codex tests, production types, task formatting, diff validation, and autoreview passed.
